caption: Newanforbi v. Derrick et al.
claims: 42 USC 1983: 1A Retaliation, 14A Equal Protection, Due Process
status: Order filed July 24, 2026 (Mag. Peterson): Palacios's MTD (Doc 24) GRANTED — failed all four Ninth Circuit state-actor tests; court flagged a misquoted Rawson v. Recovery Innovations citation in Plaintiff's opposition and issued a Rule 11(b)(2) reminder. Derrick/Noguchi's MTQ/MTD (Doc 9) GRANTED IN PART (claims dismissed) / DENIED IN PART (quash denied as moot given their waiver of service). 1A retaliation and substantive due process claims DISMISSED as to all defendants; FAC DISMISSED WITH LEAVE TO AMEND within 14 days (by August 7, 2026) — if no amendment is filed, the action proceeds solely on the Equal Protection claim against Derrick. This is in apparent, unresolved tension with Plaintiff's July 22, 2026 Notice of Voluntary Dismissal, which purported to self-execute the dismissal of both Derrick and Noguchi two days before this order; the order does not address that filing.
judge: Hon. Daniel J. Calabretta / Mag. Peterson
note: Palacios's MTD GRANTED Jul. 24; FAC dismissed w/ leave to amend by Aug. 7. Jul. 22 dismissal of Derrick/Noguchi was valid as a matter of right (no answer/MSJ served) — Jul. 24 order doesn't address it.
defendants: Andrew Derrick (#6910) — Notice of Voluntary Dismissal filed Jul. 22, 2026 (self-executing under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i)); Jul. 24, 2026 order nonetheless treats him as the sole remaining defendant if no amended complaint is filed — tension unresolved on the docket; Katie Palacios — MTD GRANTED Jul. 24, 2026 (failed all four state-actor tests); claims DISMISSED WITH LEAVE TO AMEND; Gary Noguchi (#7284) — Notice of Voluntary Dismissal filed Jul. 22, 2026 (self-executing); Jul. 24, 2026 order separately dismissed claims against him for failure to allege supervisory liability
causes: Substantive Due Process — Arbitrary Abuse of Power
key_facts: Derrick told Plaintiff at their first meeting (Jan. 2025): 'You do not have freedom of speech. Not in HOPE group you don't.' — preceded by: 'it would not be good for you if you didn't stop.' Plaintiff had been in HOPE group ~5 years despite completing all homework multiple times; group repeatedly reset due to clinician turnover. Derrick and Palacios jointly revoked the standard 10-minute grace period (Apr. 2025), stating: 'You are clearly abusing the 10-minute as an excuse to show up late.' FedEx job (Mar. 2025, $20/hr): Plaintiff was denied a scheduling accommodation and forced to resign (~Apr. 17, 2025); lost wages ≥ $1,500; ongoing ~$600/week. CTM (mid-2025): Palacios labeled Plaintiff 'ringleader' whose speech encouraged others; Derrick gave a negative oral report focused on Plaintiff's speech; Noguchi denied reassignment on the spot despite actual knowledge of the retaliatory conflict. Chilling effect documented: Plaintiff abandoned a Form 22 reassignment request when Derrick appeared and said 'You're just finding something to complain about, huh?' — Plaintiff stuttered and could not speak. Nov. 2025 Discharge Review incorporated 'disruptive'/'ringleader' characterizations; Noguchi reviewed and approved. Comparator A (white male, same HOPE program/agent): received 1–2 min home visits, casino trip approved, Derrick personally helped file grievances — no threats or escalation. Comparator B (Black male, supervised by Derrick): Derrick stated certain offenders 'should be lined up and shot'; cited out of bounds at family park gatherings → arrest and custody. Both comparators provided sworn declarations under 28 U.S.C. § 1746.
procedural_status: Complaint filed Jan. 5, 2026 (Doc 1); FAC filed Jan. 12, 2026 (Doc 5). Early service attempts defective. Jan. 30, 2026: Defendants filed MTQ/Motion to Dismiss (Doc 9); Plaintiff initiated proper service same day. Plaintiff opposed (Doc 10, Feb. 2); Defendants replied (Doc 12). Plaintiff moved for leave to file supplemental 12(b)(6) opposition (Doc 13, Feb. 20); Defendants moved to strike or, alternatively, opposed (Doc 14, Feb. 26). The same day, the Clerk separately docketed Plaintiff's motion package as Doc 15 (motion for leave, with its proposed order lodged as Doc 15-1) and Doc 16 — the substantive [Proposed] Supplemental Opposition itself, Plaintiff's merits brief opposing dismissal on 1A retaliation, substantive due process, equal protection, and declaratory relief. Plaintiff replied in support of the motion for leave and opposed the motion to strike (Doc 17, Mar. 4, 2026). Mar. 9, 2026: Plaintiff filed a declaration documenting good-faith service efforts on Palacios and actual notice to defense counsel (Doc 19); Palacios served (POS-015) same day. Mar. 19, 2026: Motion hearings before Mag. Peterson. Apr. 2, 2026: SLB stipulation extended Palacios's federal response to Apr. 6, 2026 (all defenses reserved). Apr. 6, 2026: SLB filed Motion to Dismiss FAC (Doc 24) on three grounds: (1) Palacios fails all four Ninth Circuit state-actor tests; (2) Plaintiff fails to plead protected speech or causation; (3) Substantive due process duplicates First Amendment claim. Apr. 9, 2026: Plaintiff filed Opposition to Palacios MTD, citing Rawson v. Recovery Innovations (9th Cir. 2020) as controlling authority; did not oppose dismissal of Count III if duplicative; entered Apr. 13, 2026. SLB Reply due Apr. 20, 2026. May 18, 2026: Court issued Minute Order (Doc 26) ordering MTD (Doc 24) submitted without appearance and without argument per Local Rule 230(g); 5/28/2026 hearing VACATED. Court will set oral argument only if subsequently deemed necessary. Awaiting ruling on Docs 9, 14, and 24. May 23, 2026: SLB (Van Dine) rejected Plaintiff's $85,000 global settlement demand by letter — states MTD fully briefed and submitted; claims evidence will be fatal to Plaintiff's claims at trial; notes federal cases require unanimous jury verdict; advances cross-case damages argument that Plaintiff's own sworn declaration in Matter 1 (No. 2:25-cv-1460) attributes economic and emotional distress damages to the CHP DUI arrest, not to SLB's clients. Post-briefing development: July 2, 2026 — while Doc 24 remained under submission, Stockton parole (Noguchi's unit) transferred Plaintiff's supervision to Santa Clara County one day after Plaintiff filed the related state action naming Noguchi (Matter 15, STK-CV-UPI-2026-5417), departing from the Nov. 2025 Form 1502-DR's own record of identical violations previously resolved by verbal reprimand or PACT referral; offered as further evidence of the retaliatory pattern alleged in this action. July 22, 2026: Plaintiff filed Notice of Voluntary Dismissal Without Prejudice (Fed. R. Civ. P. 41(a)(1)(A)(i)), dismissing Defendants Derrick and Noguchi from the action, without prejudice to refiling; served via CM/ECF and, to the extent required, First-Class Mail on Erick J. Rhoan (DAG, counsel for Derrick and Noguchi) and Cynthia G. Lawrence/Bryan L. Malone (SLB, counsel for Palacios) same day. The notice's own text states the legal basis: 'Plaintiff is entitled to dismiss as to these Defendants as a matter of right because neither Defendant Derrick nor Defendant Noguchi has served an answer or a motion for summary judgment in this action' — confirming the dismissal was self-executing and procedurally sound at the time filed, independent of any court order. Palacios's Motion to Dismiss (Doc 24) remains under submission before Mag. Peterson and Palacios's claims proceed on all counts of the operative FAC, expressly unaffected by the dismissal. July 24, 2026: Mag. Peterson issued a 10-page Order (Doc 31) resolving Docs 9 and 24. On Palacios: the court walked through all four Ninth Circuit state-actor tests (public function, joint action, governmental nexus, compulsion) and found Plaintiff's allegations insufficient under each; Palacios's MTD is GRANTED. The court also noted that a Rawson v. Recovery Innovations, Inc., 975 F.3d 742 (9th Cir. 2020) quotation in Plaintiff's opposition 'does not appear in Rawson' and that the case does not stand for the proposition cited, reminding Plaintiff of his Rule 11(b)(2) certification obligations. On Derrick and Noguchi: their motion to quash service is DENIED AS MOOT (they waived service in their reply brief), but their motion to dismiss is GRANTED — the First Amendment retaliation claim is dismissed for failure to plausibly allege protected speech and a causal link to any defendant's adverse action, and the claim against Noguchi independently fails for lack of supervisory-liability allegations under Hansen v. Black. The substantive due process claim is dismissed as duplicative of the First Amendment claim, per Albright v. Oliver, with Plaintiff's non-opposition. Also DENIED: Plaintiff's request for email case-activity notifications (PACER already provides this), his motion for evidence preservation and expedited discovery (no good-cause showing), and two motions for leave to file a supplemental opposition; Defendants' motion to strike is denied as moot. The operative FAC (Doc 5) is DISMISSED WITH LEAVE TO AMEND; Plaintiff may file an amended complaint within 14 days of the July 24, 2026 order (by August 7, 2026; the order's own text states the deadline as 14 days without a fixed calendar date). If no amended complaint is filed, the action proceeds solely on Plaintiff's Equal Protection claim against Derrick, and Derrick must then answer. This disposition treats Derrick and Noguchi as active parties throughout — in apparent tension with Plaintiff's July 22, 2026 Notice of Voluntary Dismissal purporting to self-execute their dismissal under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) two days earlier; the July 24 order does not reference or account for that filing, and the docket does not yet reflect how this tension resolves.
risk: Qualified immunity; rebutted by explicit on-record speech-suppression statement, documented race-based comparator disparity, and sworn third-party declarations.
